sector.narrative: Support for feminist, women-led and women's rights organisations and movements, and institutions (governmental and non-govermental) at all levels to enhance their effectiveness, influence and substainability (activities and core-funding). These organisations exist to bring about transformative change for gender equality and/or the rights of women and girls in developing countries. Their activities include agenda-setting, advocacy, policy dialogue, capacity development, awareness raising and prevention, service provision, conflict-prevention and peacebuilding, research, organising, and alliance and network building

In 2023 WGG coordinated a meeting between all the EA based partners focused on building their MEL capacity
Annual partners meeting

Kenya based participants representing Kenyan civil society and WROs attended a number of critical cross movement spaces including 2024 Feminist Leadership Movement Building and Rights Institute (FLMBaRI) led by CREA which took place in Kampala, DSROI EA (virtual); CoSP (virtual); a pre-GSWF regional conference in Kenya and AWID in Bangkok. Through engaging with WGG, a number of Kenya based organizations and actors, including but not limited to KNWD, WSA, CWID, KEFEADO represented their organizations, strong WGG politics and and forged meaningful alliances with other structurally excluded groups.

Through capacity development and inclusion programs

Nine organisations have been engaged to influence WRO to have more inclusivity and accessibility around disability rights and its intersection with Rights, and advocacy through their involvement in CREA’s training programs and consortium meetings.
Through capacity development and inclusion programs

Seven Kenya based WROs and DROs capacities were strengthened through the EA FLMBRI led by CREA in Febarury 2023. CREA's Feminist Leadership, Movement Building, and Rights Institute– East Africa (FLMBaRI-EA) is a week long residential program, designed to strengthen feminist solidarity, leadership, advocacy, and strategies for building collective power for social transformation.
Through capacity development and inclusion programs

There were significant transitions within the CREA East Africa (WGG) office, with both the Program Manager and Program Director transitioning out of the organization. These departures created a notable gap, which impacted the flow of work in the East Africa office, particularly as it took some time to fill both positions.
